tldr: Headlines are near-universally anchored to Trump's "annihilate" word — ten of eleven buckets lead with the threat or the word itself at the homepage level, making this one of the most lexically convergent headline clusters in the dataset. A secondary diplomatic frame (talks proceeding despite the rhetoric) surfaces in wire-services, Qatar, and South Africa headlines, a tension the remaining eight outlets suppress entirely. Asia Times is the only outlet to inject moral-charge language ("genocidal") into the headline itself; AfricaNews uniquely adds the ICC-attack angle.

single_outlet_findings.note: Only outlet to embed the word 'genocidal' in the headline, making the moral-charge frame visible at the homepage layer where every other outlet uses neutral threat-reporting language.
Only outlet to surface the ICC-attack angle in the headline, bundling a legality frame into the annihilation story absent from all other titles.
Uniquely structures the headline as mutual-rhetoric analysis ('Why Iran, US up rhetoric amid talks') rather than reporting the threat directly — the only explainer-mode headline in the corpus.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, Trump's 'annihilate' threat collapses a multi-track diplomatic and military story into a single threat-word spectacle across every outlet and political lean; the concurrent US-Iran talks appear in only three of eleven buckets, and the Ukraine/Zelensky dimension visible in wire-service body text is entirely absent from all homepage titles.
